tabs.title: Understanding the text
tabs.description: Read for meaning and significant details.

tabs.title: Real-life decisions
tabs.description: Apply a useful idea in a new setting.

questions.q: What do the two cousins want to do at the beach first?
choices: Buy new clothes.
Take some photos.
Visit a large museum.
Play with a toy car.
questions.explanation: The first paragraph says the cousins want to take photographs of the beach.

questions.q: Why do they decide to pick up a bag that does not belong to them?
choices: They want to give it to Eva.
They need a new bag for lunch.
They want to show it to their teacher.
It is close to the water and could become rubbish in the sea.
questions.explanation: The narrator notices that the unwanted bag is near the sea, so they collect it.

questions.q: Who explains that wind carries rubbish into the water?
choices: The narrator's brother.
The children's teacher.
Rosa from the café.
A man walking along the beach.
questions.explanation: Rosa tells the cousins that wind moves rubbish left on the beach into the sea.

questions.q: How do the cousins feel after collecting rubbish for an hour?
choices: They are tired but pleased with what they have done.
They are angry because they cannot buy drinks.
They are disappointed because they find nothing.
They are worried because they lose their bags.
questions.explanation: The fourth paragraph says that the children are hot and tired but happy.

questions.q: Why does Rosa give the children gloves?
choices: To help them take better pictures.
To help them pick up rubbish more safely.
To keep them warm in the café.
To help them swim in the sea.
questions.explanation: Rosa offers gloves and large bags after seeing that they want to collect litter.

questions.q: What is important about the cup Eva buys later?
choices: It is made of glass instead of plastic.
It is a present for Rosa.
Eva keeps it until she can put it in the bin.
Eva throws it into the sea when she is finished.
questions.explanation: Eva does not avoid every plastic item but disposes of her cup properly.

questions.q: Why could Eva's photos be useful in the café?
choices: They show that the sea has no rubbish.
They help Rosa sell more drinks.
They prove that the cousins never use plastic.
They may encourage other people to care for the beach.
questions.explanation: The final paragraph imagines other visitors seeing the photographs on the wall.

questions.q: You see a plastic bottle left on a windy beach. What would the cousins probably do?
choices: Leave it there because it is not theirs.
Put it in a suitable bin if it is safe to pick up.
Hide it under the sand so nobody sees it.
Wait until the wind moves it into the sea.
questions.explanation: The cousins choose to collect litter even when it does not belong to them.

questions.q: You buy a drink in a plastic cup. Which action best follows Eva's example?
choices: Keep the cup until you find a bin.
Drop the cup beside the café.
Throw it into the sea after drinking.
Leave it on the table for the wind.
questions.explanation: Eva's useful action is keeping the cup for proper disposal rather than littering.

questions.q: What could the photos on Rosa's wall tell visitors?
choices: The beach is always perfectly clean.
The two cousins work at the café every day.
Only children can help keep a beach clean.
Small actions can help, even if the beach is not perfect.
questions.explanation: The story ends with the possibility that their modest clean-up will inspire other visitors.
